column1: # Binaries that hand out root (or arbitrary file access) the moment they are SUID.
# Keyed on the file name, not the path, so /usr/local/bin/find and /tmp/find both match.
# Nothing in here is part of a stock set-id set - if one of these turns up in a
# find -perm -4000 hunt, someone put it there.
# risk  privesc  spawns a shell / runs commands as the file owner
#       read     reads any file as the owner (which means /etc/shadow)
#       write    writes any file as the owner (which means /etc/passwd, cron, sudoers)
#       limited  useful, but not a one-step win
